title: Adaptive compute-primitive selector with entropy-regularized latency-cost probes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an adaptive compute-primitive (kernel/op-variant) selector that performs lightweight, entropy-regularized probes to learn per-architecture and per-sequence-length latency/cost trade-offs online. The selector must coordinate with prefill/decode scheduling to avoid probing amplification during bursts and should expose telemetry to the Console for per-route cost and latency attribution. The goal is to reduce tail latency regressions and unit cost by selecting better runtime kernels for mixed-length, mixed-precision workloads while ensuring safe fallbacks under SLO pressure.
acceptance_criteria: Probe harness integrated into runtime that can run sub-millisecond microbenchmarks for a small set of candidate compute primitives without violating latency SLOs
Entropy-regularized exploration policy implemented (configurable temperature) with explicit regret/backoff when probes harm SLOs
Seqlen- and architecture-aware feature vector used in selector model (histogram bucketing or light-weight sketch) and persisted for warm-starts
Automated A/B rollout with Canary policy and telemetry showing per-variant latency, P50/P95/P99, and tokens-per-second cost delta
Unit and integration tests covering probe failure modes, fallback paths, and cache/KV-state interactions
Documentation (design doc + console doc) and a GitHub PR merged behind a feature flag
steps: Spike: microbench methodology and probe overhead budget (done)
Design doc: selector API, probe schedule, and safety knobs (draft)
Implement probe harness in runtime and offline microbench suite
Implement online selector with entropy-regularized exploration and warm-start seqlen buckets
Integrate with prefill/decode scheduler to suppress probes during burst or when KV cache warmups happen
Add telemetry hooks and Console dashboard rows for per-variant metrics
Rollout plan: feature flag -> canary -> gradual ramp -> full rollout with automatic rollback triggers

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Probes increase tail latency during bursts. Mitigation: backoff/suppress probes based on burst detector and KV-cache signals, entropy-regularized exploration
Risk: Selector oscillation between variants causing instability. Mitigation: add hysteresis and minimum-stable-window before committing variant changes
Risk: Probe results not transferable across hardware revisions. Mitigation: include architecture fingerprint and warm-start cache per-arch; fall back to conservative default if no warm-start
Risk: Observability gaps. Mitigation: add per-request metadata tagging for probe decisions and integrate into Console trace view
outcome_metrics: Target: reduce per-token unit cost by 6-12% on mixed-length web workloads within 30 days of rollout
Target: P99 latency no worse than +3% absolute compared to baseline; probe-induced regressions capped to <0.5% of requests
Target: improve compute utilization variance (across GPUs) by 8% leading to cost predictability improvements
